title: A timetable as a table
brief:
Information in rows and columns belongs in a table, not in a list. A table has a header row that says what each column means, and a screen reader can read any cell together with its column name: "Room: B12". Under the list, build a table of the lab timetable with four columns: Day, Time, Session and Room. Give it a caption, put the column names in th cells in the first row, and add one tr for each session. When the table is complete, delete the old list. ```
…
Day…
Monday…
```

vocabulary.gloss: the element for information in rows and columns
table row: one line of the table
a header cell (the name of a column) and an ordinary data cell
the title of a table, written as the first thing inside <table>

starterHtml:
Computer lab timetable

Week 7. Bring your student card: the doors are locked at 5 pm.

  • Monday, 10:00 to 12:00, Python practice, B12
  • Tuesday, 14:00 to 16:00, Academic skills, B12
  • Wednesday, 09:00 to 11:00, Maths workshop, A4
  • Thursday, 13:00 to 15:00, Web practice, B12
  • Friday, 10:00 to 11:00, Drop-in help, Library

checks.label: The first row has four header cells (th)
At least four rows of four data cells (16 or more td)

hints:
Start with the skeleton: and
, with Lab timetable, week 7 as the first line inside. Then add one … for the header row.
The header row is <tr><th>Day</th><th>Time</th><th>Session</th><th>Room</th></tr>. Each lesson is a <tr> with four <td> cells, in the same order.

Copy the five lessons from the list into five rows, one td for each piece of information, then delete everything from
    to
.
